page.layout: One page of text; a verse heading at top, then a title block and an elegy in two-line verse with the body in full width; no marginal notes visible; running head at top.

main_text.l: Sic flamma & ultrices, flammas superastis auar.
Et Deus est flammis, est quoque & victor aquæ,
Sic reliquas auidus mundi sibi subdere gentes,
Et qui alios spreuit, & vulgi fit fabula: & alta
Qui & viuens petiit, nunc maris ima petit:
main_text.head: IANO GARNERIO AVRE liis improuisa prorsus morte sublato.
Elegia VIII.
main_text.p: IBAT Ianus, & heu nimis ibat forte sinistra, Depicta cantans picta per arua lyra: Admirabantur sylua montesque sonantem, Et tacitis stabant flumina fixa vadis. Quū doluere suas Nympha non currere lymphas, Et, Nouus hic Orpheus (mox ait & na) quis est?
Dixit: & aduersum in litus transfire parantem, In medias traxit pessima Naias aquas.
Ille cadit, sinistraque absentes clamat amicos, Hei misero praesens tempore nullus erat: Aspiciunt illum sylua montesque cadentem, Cumque vocante vocant, cumque gementē gemunt.
Interea Ianus toto bibit ore procellas, Et sub aquas tandem pondere victus abit: Haud aliter, cana venit quum meta senecta, Et
Interea: the text runs on past the page end.

page.notes: Printed heading and verse lines are rendered as printed; several words in the verse block are uncertain and were not marked individually. The first lines are set in a larger italic/roman mix; some letters are unclear, notably in the Greek-influenced line "Sic flamma & ultrices" and "Et, Nouus hic Orpheus". Catchword "Et" is printed at lower right.
